title: Verifying a delivery by a shared token the provider echoes back

contract.summary: Some providers do not sign deliveries; they echo a token the subscriber chose when it subscribed. Google Calendar sends the channel's `token` back in the `X-Goog-Channel-Token` header on every notification (with an EMPTY body); Microsoft Graph sends `clientState` inside EVERY item of the notification's `value` array. Verification is a constant-time comparison of that echoed value against the connection's secret — the same refusal-by-default as HMAC (no secret configured is a failure, never an accept), and the same result shape.

functions.verifySharedToken: verifySharedToken({raw, headers, secret, scheme: {in: header, name} | {in: body, path}}) -> {ok: true} | {ok: false, reason}

contract.referenceNote: Decisions: a header name is matched case-insensitively (proxies do not preserve case); a body path is dotted, and a segment ending in `[]` means EVERY element of that array, all of which must match — one wrong item fails the whole delivery, and an empty collection carries no token; an absent, empty or non-string token is `delivery carried no token` or `token did not match`, never accepted; a body that is not JSON under a body scheme is refused as such. Reasons are fixed strings a host can log on.

cases.title: Google's channel token in the header, empty body: accepted
A lower-cased header from a proxy is the same header
An empty token header is no token
Never accept when unconfigured — an endpoint that verifies nothing looks protected

expected.reason: no shared token configured for this trigger

cases.title: An empty secret is unconfigured, not a token that happens to be empty

expected.reason: no shared token configured for this trigger

cases.title: Graph's clientState on the one notification in the batch: accepted
A batch with one wrong clientState is refused as a whole
A batch where every item carries the token is accepted
An empty `value` has nothing to compare, and nothing to compare is not a match
A body scheme on a body that is not JSON
Items without the field carry no token
A number where the token should be is a mismatch, not a coincidence
A path with no collection segment reads one value
A token that agrees on every byte but the last is refused (constant-time in both runtimes)
